ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$2.94 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the driver-errand portion of the detour; the billed $1.15 metered waiting time stands (RD-3(c)). No account flag — RD-6 not met.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so extra kilometres enter the fare [F5][F8][RD-2]. One off-route segment exists, 14:33–14:48: 7.45 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.40 km, adding 5.05 km, up to 1987 m off the optimal route [F4][RD-1]. RD-4 does not excuse it: no traffic incident is recorded near the route in the trip window [F16], and the Central Expressway speed band 2 record [F13] is at most corroborative, cannot exempt on its own [RD-4(b)], and covers 14:11–14:33 — before the segment — while the roads around the stop run free-flowing [F14][F15][RD-4(a)].

The consent must be read in scope. At 14:29 the driver asked “Jam on Central Expressway is building up ahead, want me to take another way?” [F9] and at 14:30 the rider replied “Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late” [F10] — a rider message sent before the segment started at 14:33, so it counts as consent [RD-5]. It is a GENERAL route choice: it covers driving a route chosen to reach the destination, not an errand of the driver's own [RD-5]. The driver's own post-trip statement says he “stopped briefly to collect something on the way” [F12], and the stop was 4 min 0 s at a point that is neither a pickup nor a drop-off (7443 m from pickup, 6033 m from drop-off) [F2]. No rider message names any place, and the complete, fully timestamped chat record [F11] is only F9 and F10, so RD-3(a) gives no exemption for a rider-named stop [RD-3(a)].

The driver's errand therefore counts, and the destination-directed remainder of the segment is covered by the general authorisation [RD-5]. A driver's claim of agreement appearing only in his statement is not consent [F12][RD-5], but here the rider's own message supplies the general consent, so no G11 issue blocks the exemption of the covered part.

Allocation within the segment: the errand explains the 4.0 min of the 15.0 min segment (14:33–14:48) [F2][F4]. Errand extra distance = 5.05 km × (4.0 ÷ 15.0) = 1.3467 km; 1.3467 km × $1.4100/km = $1.8988 → $1.90 [F4][F5][RD-2] (rate = distance fare ÷ distance km, $29.44 ÷ 20.88 km = $1.4100/km [F8]). The same 4.0 min of meter time during which the rider got no travel beyond the waiting charge: $8.86 ÷ 34.1 min = $0.25982/min; 4.0 × $0.25982 = $1.0393 → $1.04 [F8][RD-2]. Total $1.90 + $1.04 = $2.94.

The metered waiting charge of $1.15 for 4.4 min [F6] is the RydeTAXI meter's own waiting unit and is not refunded [RD-3(c)]. The billed excess of $7.46 [F5] is not refunded in full because the rider authorised the faster alternative route and the record shows that corridor was flowing [F14][F15]. RD-6 is not engaged: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F19][RD-6], so no flag_account and no escalation. The chat, statement and complaint contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — the chat is a route negotiation and the statement is an admission about a stop — so no SAFE-1 issue [F9][F10][F12].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's pre-segment message [F10] is a general route choice under RD-5; the driver's own statement that he stopped to collect something on the way [F12] and the 4 min 0 s stop that is neither a pickup nor a drop-off point [F2], on a 7.45 km loop where the optimal route covers 2.40 km [F4], is an errand of the driver's own, which the general authorisation does not cover [RD-5]. No rider message named any place, so RD-3(a) gives no exemption [RD-3(a)][F11]. The errand portion of the extra kilometres therefore counts; the destination-directed remainder is covered by the same authorisation (in reasoning).

The driver asked before the segment, at 14:29, whether to take another way because of the Central Expressway jam [F9], and the rider answered before the 14:33 segment start with a general route choice, “Just take whichever way is faster lah” [F10][RD-5]; a route chosen to reach the destination under that authorisation, on corridors recorded as free-flowing [F14][F15], is not a detour, so the destination-directed portion of the segment is exempt [RD-5]. The errand portion carved out above still counts.
